## Objectives {#objectives}

By the end of this session you can:

- Reconstruct the semester's pipeline map from memory.
- Name which checks caught real errors, and where.
- Carry your `checks.R` into your own research.
- State your own AI-use policy.
- Say what each tool you learned cannot see.
- Name what you will read this year that is not economics.

## What we cover {#coverage}

- The thirteen investigations, replayed as one arc.
- The verification ledger: which checks caught what, all semester.
- **The audit, revisited.** Every constructed variable this semester got
  checked against something outside itself: a gold set for the machine
  labels, a second product for the exposures, ground truth for the
  images, a hand-checked sample for the transcripts. Same move each
  time, different data. Name yours, and say what it would take to
  convince a referee.
- The `checks.R` showcase.
- The reveal: how this course was built, AI-assisted and disclosed,
  under its own policy.
- **What the tools do not replace.** Every method here has a limit. A
  model answers whether or not the question was sound. A pipeline runs
  whether or not the variable means anything. Nothing in the toolkit
  makes you careful, patient, or curious. Those decide the quality of
  the work, and they are the part nobody can automate for you.
- **Know what your instrument cannot see.** A band index does not
  measure what you wish it measured. A transcript drops what the room
  knew. A classifier's label is a prediction, not an observation. Write
  the limit into your methods section, in your own words.
- **Read outside economics.** Questions come from noticing things, and
  you notice more when you read widely. History, geography, the other
  social sciences, the domain literature of whatever you study, good
  reporting. A narrow reading list produces narrow questions. Come with
  three things you read this year that were not economics, and what
  each one made you want to measure.
- Where to take this next: the methods we skipped, and how to learn one
  on your own.

**Verification habit.** All of them. The posture is the job now.
